items.original: RES-EP13-01. v13 does NOT repair check-evaluation-proof-v6.py: EP6's inner C-2 join still runs against the DEFECTIVE check-c2.py bytes underneath EP8, and this candidate is a strictly stronger OUTER gate over an inner join it leaves unrepaired EP6 is pinned, is executed transitively, and is not repaired by this candidate; a stronger outer gate over a defective inner join is worth having and is not the same thing as repairing the inner join. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 0a7ac122a598bb7b9454b1b3c46c586f6fd551a2a1ebcf5584665f875457c5f0.
items.correction: Replace the defective transitive C-2 join with the explicit product plan/derivation DAG schema and recomputed source/Plan joins; historical EP6/8 checker bytes stay defective history.

items.original: RES-EP13-02. The answer-provenance property is NOT established against any route region that can distinguish a call this guard is measuring from a call it is not, BY ANY MEANS WHATEVER, and that answers honestly when it judges itself observed Every variant named in this document is an INSTANCE of that class and never its definition, and no set or count published here bounds it A-9 removes one means of distinguishing and is a NARROWING, NOT A CLOSURE THIS IS THE BOUNDARY and the banner is scoped by it. IR-EP12-01 rejected the predecessor for publishing an ENUMERATION of three variant names in this position: a reader told that only a frame read or a cell read breaks the green performs a cheap grep, excludes it, and draws a false conclusion. What is published now is the CAPABILITY that defeats the property. Reading this guard's frame or its servers' cells is one means; comparing the seat object against the one seen on the region's own first call is a second and needs no introspection at all; counting the ledger entries the region's own call produces is a third and compares no binding at all; there are others nobody here has thought of. The variants below are BUILT AND EXECUTED on every ordinary run and what they demonstrate is that the class is real, not that it is bounded. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: AX6-stack-walking-witness-forgery, AX9-obfuscated-witness-forgery, MD5-observed-window-discrimination-by-ledger-entry-count, RX2c-unenumerated-witness-forgery.
items.correction: No answer-provenance claim against adversarial Python route regions. Product host/evaluator is an explicit authenticated first-party TCB; untrusted inputs are inert typed data. Replay verifies reproducibility under that boundary.

items.original: RES-EP13-03. The corpus carries seven pinned vectors over ONE distinct PlanIntent, so every value-equality result here is a measurement over that one subject and is not an equivalence proof between the two instruments Every value-equality result in this document — A-1, A-7, the differential oracle and the whitelisting that every answer-substitution variant relies on — inherits that limit. The two instruments agree at every position except four on this census, which is why a region that routes those four honestly satisfies every value rule there is. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 7 pinned vectors x 3 imported APIs = 21 answers.
items.correction: The seven-vector measurement remains a finite historical measurement, never an equivalence proof. Product conformance requires independent source/semantic cases; reference counts confer no universal property.

items.original: RES-EP13-04. The introspection tripwire is an ENUMERATION of identifiers, it supports NO published property, it is not a scored guard, and a variant spelled with identifiers it does not name is measured escaping it on every run IR-EP11-02 found it blocking that an enumeration of spellings was the sole guard for a class. The repair was to stop counting the enumeration as a guard rather than to lengthen it, and that repair is structural: GUARD_REGISTRY publishes scored=false for it. It still produces a finding and therefore still gates the exit code, which is a different statement from affecting a property, and IR-EP12-NB-05 is right that the distinction deserves saying. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: MD5-observed-window-discrimination-by-ledger-entry-count, RX2c-unenumerated-witness-forgery.
items.correction: No identifier tripwire is an authority guard in the product. Closed input schemas and authenticated selected code replace the attempted same-process hostile-code containment.

items.original: RES-EP13-05. This checker reads its own source for its AST scans and its own bytes are not a verified snapshot of anything: a checker cannot pin itself, and every scan it runs over itself is therefore evidence about the file on disk at read time and nothing more Every AST scan this instrument runs over itself is therefore evidence about the bytes on disk at the moment it read them, and the trust order — inert bytes, SHA-256 verify, execute from the verified snapshot, never a second disk read — applies to everything else this file loads and cannot apply to this file. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: own bytes in own pin table: False.
items.correction: Reviewer pins are produced outside the author instrument; the frozen reviewed snapshot is the review subject. A checker does not authenticate itself or mutable files by scanning its own source.

items.original: RES-EP13-06. MEASURED, NOT REPAIRED: the canonical unsigned decimal defect is measured here and left in place, and repairing it is the EP5 successor's obligation and not this candidate's The defect is in the EP5 lineage's canonical encoding and it is measured here so that a successor cannot claim it was never seen. Measuring a defect and leaving it in place is honest; measuring it and publishing it as repaired is what this corpus keeps rejecting. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 1ccc12c347f0c7598604227179a2ba0cc461466657908b5c5f9645db4f7b99e2.
items.correction: Product canonical admission rejects float/exponent/negative-zero and distinguishes bool/int; exact byte encoding and independent preimage vectors replace the unsigned decimal encoder defect.

items.original: RES-EP13-07. MEASURED, NOT REPAIRED: positions that move durable identity beneath a byte-identical EvaluationAuthoritySealRef are measured and published here and left in place; repairing them is the v6/v8 successors' obligation Regime B's admitted set contains positions that move durable identity, and a subset of those move it while the EvaluationAuthoritySealRef stays byte-identical, which is the shape that makes a seal a poor witness for the thing it seals. Both counts are recomputed by execution on every run rather than transcribed. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 3 of 5 identity-moving positions.
items.correction: Product seal binds Plan, execution plan, evidence, evaluator, policy, proof and verdict. Every identity-moving semantic input reaches Plan/proof/seal/Run; wrong-Plan and rehashed false-proof cases refuse.

items.original: RES-EP13-08. The distinct-intent family drives 14 intents, which is a MEASUREMENT over the intents built here and is not a proof about the space of PlanIntents A family of fourteen distinct intents discriminates more than one intent does and less than the space does. The number is published so that the difference between those two statements is visible. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 14 distinct intents.
items.correction: The fourteen-intent family is retained as a bounded historical measurement. No product proof of all possible PlanIntents is claimed; current schemas/joins and implementation conformance are explicit.

items.original: RES-EP13-09. Provenance is not correctness: these rules establish that the answer used is check-c2-v4.py's answer, and establish NOTHING about whether check-c2-v4.py is right If the repaired instrument is itself wrong, A-1 through A-9 certify that its wrong answer is faithfully the one used, and RES-EP13-15 records that its own published self-census is under a blocking adjudication today. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 54ff764d155f5582bc66fd7bf8138b7eaed5f90f46b92975c4bc7a85ffb3df17.
items.correction: Provenance is explicitly distinct from correctness. Authenticated report custody is followed by independent oracle comparisons, and product qualification requires real native measurements.

items.original: RES-EP13-10. The own-constant-leaf battery cannot re-run itself, so the four counters it publishes about its own execution are not re-derived by the nested runs and are silently admitted under a float spelling; this is measured and enumerated by position on every TOP-LEVEL run The battery injects True, False and 1.0 at every int/bool leaf of the candidate and re-runs the whole checking layer per case. It cannot re-run itself, so the four counters it publishes about its own execution are not re-derived by the nested runs. Those four positions are enumerated by name rather than counted, because a count is not a record. This residual is TEXT-ONLY because a test bound to the battery's own output would pass on hollow text by construction.
items.correction: Candidate self-counters do not decide product admission. Exact schema typing precedes evaluation; reference reports are observations, not authority over their own semantics.

items.original: RES-EP13-11. check-completeness.py and check-rust-provider-protocol-v4.py both pre-exist this candidate and neither references it check-completeness.py exits 1 with BOTH findings open: IR-C2V4-01 on the C-2 surface row, and R2-FINAL-03 as the one cross-cutting open finding, and each independently drives exit 1 check-rust-provider-protocol-v4.py exits 1 because there is no rg binary on this host Neither failure is attributable to this candidate and neither checker references it. This residual is TEXT-ONLY-NOT-MECHANICALLY-ENFORCEABLE because this instrument cannot measure another checker's exit code from inside its own process, and the predecessor's version of this residual demonstrated exactly what that costs: it asserted that the cause had moved from R2-FINAL-03 to IR-C2V4-01, that was wrong, and two parties measured it wrong independently. RET-EP13-06 retracts it. The corrected statement is carried in this residual's enforced anchors so that hollowing the prose cannot lose it again.
items.correction: Historical checker failures remain recorded by cause. The product successor has its own pinned subject and acceptance; it does not re-label either old checker as passing or close blind litmus by prose.

items.original: RES-EP13-12. Where the answer-provenance guard is the SOLE GUARD for a variant, that is measured and published per variant rather than asserted, because a sole guard nobody has declared is an undisclosed single point of failure The per-variant sole-guard rows are recomputed every run and published in full. Where a variant is caught by exactly one guard, that guard is a single point of failure for that class, and a reader is entitled to know which classes rest on one mechanism. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: AX2-decoy-call-superseded-answer (answerProvenance), AX4-commitment-only-substitution (answerProvenance), AX8-differential-sentinel-detector (answerProvenance), MD2-observed-window-discrimination-appended-ledger-repair (answerProvenance), MD3-observed-window-discrimination-overwritten-ledger-repair (answerProvenance), MD4-observed-window-discrimination-originals-compared (answerProvenance), RX1-seat-substitution-declared-accessor (answerProvenance), RX3-seat-wrapping-of-the-guards-own-server (answerProvenance), RX4-stale-anchored-object-replay (answerProvenance).
items.correction: No sole Python answer-provenance guard is carried into product authority. Trusted pure evaluation and explicit inert-data admission replace that threat boundary; correctness still needs qualification.

items.original: RES-EP13-13. Guard measurements are order-dependent unless the injector deep-copies the value it injects, and this run measures that no guard mutated a shared injection-table member The claim is structural, not accidental, and the earlier review had nothing to catch IR-EP11-NB-03 asked whether the predecessor's shared-table hazard had ever had an instance. The injection-isolation probe drives the guards over the mutable hostile values and measures whether any of them mutated the table member it was handed. It is published as a measurement of a hazard that has not occurred, not as a repair of one that did. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 280 injections through 3 guards mutated [].
items.correction: New mutation/reference cases deep-copy hostile inputs before invoking the model. This is fixture isolation only; no claim that a Python program is sandboxed.

items.original: RES-EP13-14. The differential oracle is asymmetric: it discriminates strongly on validate_plan_intent and weakly on plan_intent_commitment, so its cardinality is a property of this census and not of the instruments It discriminates strongly on the validation verdict and weakly on the commitment, so its discriminating cardinality is a property of this census and of these two instruments, and an evasion that routes the divergent positions honestly agrees with it everywhere. That is why it is published as NOT SUFFICIENT ALONE. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 1656 enumerated cases.
items.correction: The old differential census is not used as an equivalence proof or a release oracle. Product independent oracle/corpus and replay obligations are named separately.

items.original: RES-EP13-15. check-c2-v4.py's own published self-census is under a BLOCKING adjudication today, IR-C2V4-01, and this candidate does not re-pin onto check-c2-v5.py to escape it The defect is in v4's measurement of its own counters and not in the admission API this join depends on Chasing the adjudication onto check-c2-v5.py would re-pin this join onto a moving target mid-review, and the corpus float sweep records v5 admitting 13 of 66 integer leaves behind a byte-identical green banner, so v5 is not obviously the safer pin. The pinned bytes are recorded by digest either way. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 54ff764d155f5582bc66fd7bf8138b7eaed5f90f46b92975c4bc7a85ffb3df17.
items.correction: The old C-2 v4 self-census is not elevated. Product plan/derivation identity schemas and retained mutation tests are the prospective alternative under D-372; independent review must examine their bytes.

items.original: RES-EP13-16. A-2 and A-9 hold only inside a window this guard opens; outside such a window the answer is bound by VALUE and not by object identity, so a substitution outside it is DETECTED, NOT PREVENTED A region that behaves differently when observed is bounded here only by A-7's value agreement, by A-6's identity checks and by A-9's hidden window, and by nothing stronger On this corpus the two instruments agree everywhere except four positions, so a region that routes those four honestly satisfies every value rule there is This is the honest cost of the design and it is stated beside the rules rather than beneath them. A-9 narrows it: there is now a window the region cannot see, so a region that discriminates by reading bindings answers dishonestly inside a measured window and is reported. It does not remove it: a region that never reads a binding is bounded by value alone exactly as before, and MD5 is built to make that concrete rather than to leave it as a caveat. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 21 of 21 unanchored answers.
items.correction: No observed-window value/provenance guarantee is retained. The entire callable evaluator is trusted selected code; producer-supplied flags cannot bypass independent replay.

items.original: RES-EP13-17. Two residuals are declared text-only and not mechanically enforceable because this instrument has no in-process measurement to bind them to, and declaring that is honest where inventing a test that would pass on hollow text is not Declaring a residual text-only is a worse outcome than binding it and a better outcome than inventing a test that would pass on hollow text. The text-only ids are declared in the CHECKER rather than in this document, so a bound residual cannot be demoted to an unbound one by editing the artifact. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 17 of 19 residuals bound to a measurement, 2 text-only.
items.correction: Text-only historical disclosures remain text-only. Product design review examines meaning directly; no padding/anchor counter is claimed to mechanically establish architectural completeness.

items.original: RES-EP13-18. A-9's hidden window is invisible to a region that reads bindings, and it is NOT invisible to a region that reads the ledger wrapper's own closure cell, nor to one that counts the ledger entries its own call produces The anchor's internal calls do not re-enter the shared ledger, and that difference is a side channel this instrument measures rather than denies: MD5 uses it and escapes The hidden window works by writing the contents of a closure cell that the ledger's own wrapper holds, which is a thing this guard can do and a region can observe if it looks there. It is also detectable without looking anywhere: an unobserved commitment call re-enters the ledger for its internal canonical call and an anchor-served one does not, so the entry delta says whether anyone is measuring. MD5 is that region, it is built and executed on every ordinary run, and it escapes every scored guard while routing every pinned commitment to the superseded encoder. Publishing the side channel beside the rule that has it is the only way a reader can price the rule. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 3 observability variants caught by A-9, 1 measured escaping it.
items.correction: No hidden-window mechanism is retained, so ledger-entry-count discrimination is not a claimed containment boundary. The product explicitly excludes hostile code in the trusted evaluator process.

items.original: RES-EP13-19. Residual anchors are now LOAD-BEARING SENTENCES rather than short tokens, so a residual gutted to its anchors and padded to length is still the disclosure rather than a stub This does not stop an author writing the anchors and then padding them with contradictory prose, and no mechanical rule inside a checker can; binding is not meaning IR-EP12-NB-02 gutted six of the predecessor's residuals to their anchors plus their bound number plus padding, and the checker stayed green each time, because the anchors were short tokens like ROUTE REGION and AX6 that survive any amount of hollowing and mean nothing on their own. Here the anchors are the sentences that carry the disclosure and every residual's anchors must total at least 55% of its declared minimum length, which this checker measures about its own table and publishes. Gutting a residual to its anchors now leaves the disclosure standing. MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 5073 anchor characters across 19 residuals, 0 below 55% of their declared minimum.
items.correction: Independent semantic review is required. A prose-anchor checker cannot establish that surrounding text is truthful; source pins and passing counts do not replace that review.
